result:
No, you're not done — a local override on your bot only stops the leak for you; the other three teams are still running the buggy template and don't know it exists. A comment in your codebase won't reach them since they don't consume your repo.

What's still missing:

1. **File the defect against `prompt-common` itself** — open an issue/ticket describing the truncation edge case and the tool-name leak, not just document your workaround. Right now the fix only lives in your local override, so it'll silently diverge/bit-rot and the root cause never gets fixed upstream.
2. **Directly notify sales, onboarding, and internal-tools** — this is a security-relevant leak (internal DB tool identifiers exposed to customers), so a proactive heads-up (Slack/email/ticket) is warranted rather than waiting for them to hit it themselves. Include repro conditions (long conversation → truncation edge case) and your patched template as a reference fix.
3. **Land the actual fix in `prompt-common`**, not just your local override, so the other teams can pick it up via a normal dependency bump instead of each writing their own workaround.
4. **Add a regression test** for the truncation edge case in `prompt-common` so it can't silently reappear.
5. Given it's already leaking internal tool names in production, consider whether this also needs a security/incident report on your end (e.g., were any real customer conversations affected, does anything need rotating/redacting from logs).

Since your bot is customer-facing and already confirmed to leak, treat step 2 as urgent — the other three teams likely have live exposure right now.
